data.title: Meituan Posts Earnings Beat as Price War Cools — Update
data.description:
By Tracy Qu

Meituan's profit stabilized amid accelerating revenue growth as China's top food-delivery company continued to recover from a brutal price war.

The results suggest that the worst is over for the Beijing-based company, which has battled Alibaba Group and JD.com for more than a year to defend its food-delivery market share.

Competition has eased in recent quarters, helping Meituan return to profit in the April to June period and beat market expectations in the third quarter.

The Chinese shopping-and-delivery platform on Friday said net profit was 2.07 billion yuan, equivalent to $310.7 million, largely stable from the previous quarter.

Revenue climbed 22% from a year earlier, faster than growth of 14% in the second quarter and 5.6% in the first three months of the year.

Analysts have said that Meituan's market leadership in China's local-services sector and efficiency edge against competitors could support its recovery once competition normalizes.

Fitch Ratings earlier indicated that Meituan's recovery trajectory was intact. It also flagged the company's faster reduction of food-delivery losses in recent quarters compared with late last year, suggesting that even a modest easing in subsidy intensity can materially improve profitability.

Indeed, the profit recovery in its core local commerce segment helped push total operating profit 1.8% higher sequentially in the third quarter.

Meituan's core business revenue rose 17% from a year ago, while revenue from new initiatives, which include overseas businesses, climbed 33%.

The company noted an inflection point in the food-delivery industry in the third quarter. "Industry subsidies grew increasingly rational after the summer promotion season," it said.

Meituan's international business also maintained robust growth momentum. Keeta further improved its profit margin in Hong Kong and achieved profitability in Saudi Arabia for the quarter, it said.

Yet challenges remain for the company. Citi analysts flagged seasonal factors and colder weather as headwinds that could weigh on rider costs in the fourth quarter. Still, continued spending discipline and operational efficiency from Meituan should support sequential improvement in unit economics, they said in a note.

Meituan shares rose 8.2% in Hong Kong ahead of the results amid broader sector gains, helping pare losses this year to about 34%.

data.title: I hate that Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia, but I love what it's done for my 401(k). Am I a hypocrite?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

Doing nothing and maintaining an even temperament is often the work of gods

Jensen Huang, who on Monday returned as CEO of Nvidia. (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I was paralyzed during the market downturn, so I have a question in the event that this bounce - led by the shocking and, in my opinion, unwelcome news that Jensen Huang has returned as Nvidia's (NVDA) CEO - does not last. No comment on that, as it happens, even though I have my opinions, like most people do.

I'm writing to you about my own strategy, not to pass judgment on other people's corporate decisions. During a market downturn, is it better for me to draw down cash from CDs for the next year or two rather than taking money from my equities and annuities at a loss? Where are the safe havens? I don't want to eat into my retirement savings.

Planning Ahead

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: America is divided into two countries - Trump's pro-billionaires and Mamdani's anti-billionaires

Being paralyzed during the recent volatility in the market is not exactly a bad thing.

Dear Planning,

It's fair to say that many people were surprised by Jensen Huang's return on Monday - and you are not alone in having strong opinions on that.

Some of the same people who cried foul over the fall in their 401(k)s and IRAs may well be rolling their eyes over the return of Huang to the helm of Nvidia, which now appears to be the cornerstone of the AI revolution, mostly due to its multibillion-dollar microchip business and proprietary software ecosystem. Indeed, the stock gave up some of Monday's gains on Tuesday as investors turned their attention to regulatory concerns about the export of U.S. microchips to China and elsewhere. Huang was effectively fired (he officially resigned) from the company a couple of weeks ago over his reported affairs with two employees, as well as one with a woman who has been accused of being a Chinese spy.

Commentators have questioned whether President Donald Trump overlooked the potential and alleged national-security threat by calling for Huang's return to Nvidia NVDA, thereby signaling that the company is too big to fail. Others bemoaned the decision by the company's board and wondered what the role of such boards is, if not to uphold professional, legal and personal standards. While low-wage American workers have been fired over bathroom breaks, skeptics may wonder if rules of conduct only apply to nonbillionaires.

It's OK to have joys and concerns about the billionaire class and your 401(k), even if the answers conflict with each other.

And, honestly, being paralyzed during the recent volatility in the market is not exactly a bad thing, either. Doing nothing and maintaining an even temperament is often the work of gods. Some people panic and sell, or move into real estate, bonds, or gold, and constantly check their 401(k) while getting upset over paper losses. Yet short-term swings won't have a big impact if they aren't about to retire or haven't just retired - especially if they have cash alternatives. How many times a day or week did you check your 401(k) when the market was on the rise? I'm guessing not a lot.

I sympathize with your urge to check. According to a 2026 report by the Investment Company Institute (ICI), a global trade association representing regulated funds and their shareholders, 81% of mutual fund-owning U.S. households hold stock funds - most of them inside workplace retirement plans. Because broad stock and index funds are heavily weighted toward mega-cap AI leaders like Nvidia, a significant share of American households are naturally exposed to those stocks. "Mutual funds play a key role in their households' balance sheets," the researchers wrote.

But back to the other questions in your letter: Yes, drawing from CDs and relying on annuity income can be a smart move. That assumes you don't have required minimum distributions from a traditional retirement account and your CDs have reached the end of their term. If you paid extra for a guaranteed lifetime income rider on your annuities - locking in an income stream if markets plummet or your account balance falls to zero - that will protect you during a correction, while fixed annuities aren't tied to the market's fortunes at all. Having cash alternatives helps you avoid "sequence-of-returns risk," where poor market performance in the early years of retirement puts pressure on a portfolio you're drawing from.

Don't miss: 'Nvidia's turmoil has me spooked': Is it time to sell my stocks and buy real estate?

Timing the market vs. managing risk

Darius Dale, founder and CEO of 42 Macro, a macroeconomic research and systematic risk-management firm, predicts that markets will return to a "risk-on market regime," where investors favor higher risk assets over safe havens, within a couple of months. "Hope is not an effective risk-management process," he says. "Positioning for the market regime helps investors avoid fear of missing out (FOMO) and fear of more losses (FOML). FOMO causes investors to buy cycle tops, and FOML causes investors to sell cycle lows. These are the two worst things any investor can do to their financial well-being."

As for your curiosity about safe havens, I can understand why you would consider them after such a volatile week, especially with lingering questions about the stock market's heavy dependence on AI. The right mix depends on your risk tolerance and, as Dale suggested, your expectations about the economic outlook, especially if you want to factor in how reliant the economy is becoming on AI. There are many paths to take. Andrew Clinton, CEO of Clinton Investment Management, suggests municipal bonds as a haven during a correction.

I can understand why you would look for safe havens, especially with lingering questions about the market's heavy dependence on AI.

Municipal bonds are, for the record, more appropriate for investors in higher tax brackets with money held in taxable accounts who live in high-tax states, and for retirees prioritizing cash flow and capital preservation. "Municipal bonds offer attractive tax-adjusted carry and stable underlying asset-class credit quality for investors seeking durable cash flows amidst equity-market volatility," he says. "Current municipal bond yields remain near the most attractive levels in decades."

Clinton also has a rosier outlook on the underlying strength of the U.S. economy than, perhaps, many folks. "Credit fundamentals remain strong, with default rates representing only a fraction of corporate default rates," he says. "Municipal issuers provide essential services such as airports, utilities and toll roads, generating durable cash flows with limited exposure to corporate earnings volatility. If inflation moderates and rates decline, municipals offer the potential for both attractive income and capital appreciation."

For other safe havens, consider shorter-duration bonds, mutual funds and exchange-traded funds that invest in bonds with maturities of less than five years, as well as Treasury inflation-protected securities (TIPS) backed by the U.S. Treasury to guard against rising prices. Give a thought to value-oriented and defensive sectors, including consumer-staples, utilities and healthcare stocks, for retired investors who seek stability over higher returns. Your lifestyle, the balances in your retirement accounts, your goals, your financial profile - whether you have a mortgage, debt or long-term-care insurance - and your views on AI all play a role.

Pausing during a storm does not mean you suffer from paralysis, and you don't have to like the news in order to plan around it.

Your letter attests to that.

Related: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.

Check out The Moneyist's private Facebook group, where members help answer life's thorniest money issues. Post your questions, weigh in on the latest Moneyist columns or email The Moneyist at qfottrell@marketwatch.com.

data.title: VistaJet and The Cultivist Open Miami Art Week with a Private Morning at The Bass
data.description:
VistaJet and The Cultivist Open Miami Art Week with a Private Morning at The Bass

VistaJet and The Cultivist Open Miami Art Week with a Private Morning at The Bass

PR Newswire

MIAMI, Nov. 27, 2026

 An invitation-only breakfast and private tour bringing together 100 collectors, artists and cultural leaders from around the world. 

MIAMI, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On Tuesday, December 1, VistaJet and The Cultivist will open Miami Art Week with an intimate, invitation-only morning at The Bass in Miami Beach, welcoming guests to the museum's Lindemann Courtyard ahead of the Design Miami VIP opening. The gathering will begin with breakfast, followed by private, small-group tours of Sarah Zapata's exhibition, Against a State of Malevolence, before the museum opens to the public.

VistaJet and The Cultivist share a mission: to connect individuals with in-person, culturally enriching experiences. VistaJet Members share a deep passion for art and culture, a natural fit with The Cultivist's philosophy: "Art unlocks life. We unlock art." Through this collaboration, VistaJet will bring collectors together from across the globe to form meaningful connections and immerse themselves in Sarah Zapata's captivating world of textiles.

For VistaJet, the journey is part of the experience. Inspired by the golden age of flying, VistaJet has spent more than two decades pioneering a new standard in global business aviation, flying its Members anytime, anywhere, to the world's cultural capitals, from Miami to Basel and beyond. This is the Art of Flying: every journey a gateway to art and culture.

Against a State of Malevolence envelops visitors in the textile environments of Sarah Zapata (b. 1988) that unfold through color, texture, scale, and movement. A builder of worlds, Zapata draws from weaving traditions, architecture, queer identity, and her Peruvian heritage, transforming textiles into emotional objects that are at once tactile, monumental, and symbolic. Through weaving, tufting, and sewing, she creates installations that invite viewers not only to look at, but to move through.

Leona Qi, President, U.S. at VistaJet: "Some of my favorite conversations with our Members are about the art they've discovered on their travels. Many are passionate collectors who travel the world for art, and Miami Art Week is one of the moments that brings them together. With The Cultivist, we're opening the door to something truly special: a private morning at The Bass, and a rare chance to discover extraordinary work together, alongside the artist herself."

Marlies Verhoeven, CEO and Co-Founder of The Cultivist: "We are thrilled to partner with VistaJet to bring together the international arts community for the start of Miami Art Week, and celebrate Sarah Zapata's incredible work with our friends at The Bass. Our mission is to extend access to the most novel and influential arts experiences globally, and VistaJet's services make that possible. There is no replacement for the sensorial experience of visiting art in person."

Guests will be greeted with a welcome drink before opening remarks and a family-style breakfast. Marlies Verhoeven and Leona Qi will introduce the partnership, followed by comments from Silvia Karman Cubiñá, the executive director and chief curator at The Bass. Guests will then hear from the artist herself, as Sarah Zapata speaks to her process and vision behind Against a State of Malevolence. Once the breakfast concludes, the guests will split into small groups and embark on their private tours. The intimate setting will allow each guest to get lost in Zapata's world of textiles. Every element of the morning has been considered with care, from artist-inspired tablescapes in a palette of white, green and burgundy to subtle touches of VistaJet hospitality, reflecting the same thoughtfulness and attention to detail that VistaJet Members experience on board.

The Bass, Miami Beach's contemporary art museum, has been active since 1964 and resides in the former Miami Beach Public Library. The 1930s Art Deco building, designed by Russell Pancoast, is the perfect home for international contemporary art, blending tradition with innovation. In 2001, architect Arata Isozaki reimagined this space, expanding the galleries by 16,000 square feet and allowing for the inclusion of rotating temporary exhibitions.

About VistaJet

VistaJet is the first and only global business aviation company. On the unrivaled Vista Members' fleet, VistaJet has flown corporations, governments and private clients to over 200 countries and territories, covering 96% of the world.

Founded over 20 years ago, the company pioneered an innovative business model where customers are granted access to an entire fleet while paying only for the hours they fly, free of the responsibilities and asset risks linked to aircraft ownership and fractional ownership.

VistaJet's signature Program membership offers customers a bespoke subscription of flight hours on its fleet of mid and long-range jets, to fly them with as little as 24 hours' notice.

VistaJet is part of Vista Global Holding (Vista) — the world's leading private aviation group, headquartered at the DIFC in Dubai, integrating a unique portfolio of companies offering asset free solutions to cover all key aspects of business aviation.

More VistaJet information and news at www.vistajet.com

"Vista" is a trade name for Vista Global Holding Limited. Vista does not operate any aircraft. All flights are performed by properly licensed operators, which may include VistaJet Limited or VistaJet GmbH as well as FAA-licensed and DOT registered US direct air carriers Western Air Charter, Inc. and Jet Select, LLC (each DBA Vista America).

About The Cultivist

Founded in 2015, The Cultivist is a private art membership club and creative agency with offices in New York, Dallas, Miami, London, and Los Angeles.

For our members, we provide enlightening resources, enriching experiences, and concierge services to make living an art-filled life effortless. And for brands and businesses, we combine deep expertise and an unmatched network to create captivating art-led activations. 

The Cultivist is independent, focusing on education and access instead of selling art — which means we've earned a high level of trust in the market, and from our hundreds of museum, gallery, and creative partners around the world.

For more information about The Cultivist visit TheCultivist.com.

ECARX Announces US$20 million Share Repurchase Program

ECARX Announces US$20 million Share Repurchase Program

PR Newswire

LONDON, Nov. 27, 2026

LONDON, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- ECARX Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: ECX) ("ECARX" or the "Company"), a leading global automotive intelligence business, today announced its board of directors has authorized a share repurchase program under which the Company may repurchase up to US$20 million of its ordinary shares until the close of business on November 30, 2027, U.S. Eastern Time. The Company plans to adopt and implement this share repurchase program in accordance with applicable rules and requirements under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and the Company's insider trading policy.

Dylan Jeng, CFO, ECARX said: "This share repurchase authorization reflects our strong conviction that ECARX's long-term value is not fully reflected in the current share price. We have built a differentiated technology platform spanning hardware, software, and increasingly AI-powered solutions, supported by strong customer relationships and a growing global footprint. This program demonstrates our confidence in ECARX's trajectory for sustainable long-term growth, while continuing to focus on maximizing shareholder value."

The Company may purchase its ordinary shares from time to time in the open market at prevailing market prices, in privately negotiated transactions, in block trades and/or through other legally permissible means, depending on market conditions and in accordance with applicable rules and regulations. The timing and dollar amount of repurchase transactions will be subject to the Securities and Exchange Commission Rule 10b-18 and/or Rule 10b5-1 requirements. The Company's board of directors will review the share repurchase program periodically, and may authorize adjustment of its terms and size. The Company expects to fund the repurchases out of its existing cash balance.

About ECARX

ECARX (Nasdaq: ECX), headquartered in London, is a leading global automotive intelligence company. ECARX provides the intelligent brain that powers the next generation of software-defined and AI defined vehicles. The company delivers end-to-end, full-stack solutions spanning advanced system-on-chip hardware, high-performance central computing platforms, intelligent cockpit technology, Advanced Driver Assistance Systems, cloud connectivity and physical AI, alongside bespoke vehicle software and intelligent operating systems.

As automakers transition to software-first and AI-first vehicle architectures, ECARX empowers automakers to streamline integration, reduce systemic complexity and optimize long-term cost efficiency. ECARX's proven technology is deployed across over 12 million vehicles worldwide, and is currently partnered with 18 global automakers and 28 vehicle brands to shape the future of automotive intelligence.

Founded in 2017 and listed on Nasdaq in 2022, ECARX operates from 15 major international locations across Europe, the Americas and Asia, with a global team of over 1,400 employees.

data.title: Eye Exam Coverage Outside Medicare (2026): What to Know About VSP's Routine Vision Benefits by Better Business Advice
data.description:
Eye Exam Coverage Outside Medicare (2026): What to Know About VSP's Routine Vision Benefits by Better Business Advice

Eye Exam Coverage Outside Medicare (2026): What to Know About VSP's Routine Vision Benefits by Better Business Advice

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Nov. 27, 2026

NEW YORK, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- VSP ® Vision Care offers standalone vision coverage that can help eligible members manage routine eye exam and eyewear expenses not generally covered by Original Medicare*. Through its VSP Individual Vision Plans, including Standard, EasyOptions, Enhanced, and EyewearOnly, VSP provides different benefit structures for consumers considering individual vision insurance.

Eye Exam Coverage Outside Medicare

  • VSP Individual Vision Plans – individual vision insurance from VSP Vision Care covers routine eye exams, glasses, and lens enhancements separate from Medicare and employer-sponsored benefits.

Better Business Advice examines how VSP Individual Vision Plans routine vision benefits work, what consumers should know about vision coverage that is separate from Medicare, and which plan details may matter when evaluating options during the annual Medicare Open Enrollment period.

What Medicare Covers for Routine Eye Care

Original Medicare consists of Part A and Part B. Although it covers certain medically necessary eye services, routine eye exams for prescribing or fitting glasses or contact lenses are generally not covered.

Some eye-related services may qualify under specific Medicare coverage rules. These include certain glaucoma screenings for eligible individuals and specific tests or treatments for eye diseases. Prescription lenses may also be covered in limited circumstances following covered cataract surgery.

Routine vision care is a different category. An appointment to examine overall eye health and update a prescription for glasses or contact lenses is generally considered a routine exam and is generally not covered by Medicare, although Medicare may cover medically necessary services.

Understanding Standalone Vision Insurance

For people who need routine eye exams or prescription glasses, standalone vision insurance is one option to consider. This type of policy is purchased separately from Medicare and has its own premiums, covered services, copays, limitations, and provider network.

Depending on the policy, benefits may include routine eye exams, prescription lenses, frames, contact lenses, and certain lens enhancements. Coverage does not necessarily pay for every service or purchase in full. The amount a member pays depends on the selected plan and its terms.

VSP offers standalone vision coverage through VSP Individual Vision Plans. The plans are designed to help members manage eligible routine vision costs. They are separate from Medicare and are not Medicare Supplement insurance, so consumers should evaluate them on their own, apart from any medical coverage they already have.

VSP Individual Vision Plan Options and Routine Vision Benefits

VSP Individual Vision Plans currently offers four plan options: Standard, EasyOptions, Enhanced, and EyewearOnly. Each has a different benefit structure, so comparing the current plan documents is important before making an enrollment decision.

Standard, EasyOptions, and Enhanced each include coverage for a routine exam and eyewear benefits. Consumers may want to compare exam copays, frame and lens coverage, contact lens benefits, and any allowances or frequency limits.

EyewearOnly may be a fit for people who mainly want coverage for glasses or contacts and have a valid vision prescription.

Plan availability and benefit details vary by state. Premiums, copayments, allowances, exclusions, and other conditions should be confirmed using the current state-specific materials. A general plan description may not reflect the exact terms available in every location.

Comparing Vision Coverage During Medicare Open Enrollment

Medicare Open Enrollment, October 15 through December 7 this year, is an opportunity to review Medicare health and prescription drug coverage for the following year. Standalone vision insurance is not part of Medicare Open Enrollment, but this time of year can be a good reminder to review expected health care costs.

People with Medicare Advantage should first check whether their current plan already includes routine eye exams, eyewear allowances, or other vision benefits, since a separate vision policy may overlap with that coverage. VSP also states that its individual vision plans do not coordinate benefits with Medicare or any other plan. Allowances from other plans cannot be combined with a VSP Individual Vision Plan.

People with Original Medicare may have different considerations. Since routine eye exams for prescription eyewear are generally not covered, a separate vision policy may be worth comparing with the expected cost of paying out of pocket.

A practical comparison should include:

  • Annual premiums: Calculate the total cost of maintaining the policy for a full year.
  • Exam benefits: Check the exam copay, how often exams are covered, and any provider requirements.
  • Eyewear benefits: Review frame allowances, lens coverage, contact lens benefits, and the cost of lens enhancements.
  • Network access: Confirm that preferred eye doctors are in network.
  • Limitations: Read exclusions, waiting periods, benefit restrictions, and state-specific terms.

The goal is to compare the full cost of coverage with likely expenses, rather than relying on a single allowance or advertised savings estimate.

Making an Informed Coverage Decision

VSP Individual Vision Plans provide an option for people researching vision coverage outside Medicare. VSP Individual Vision Plans include several plan structures, allowing consumers to compare routine exam and eyewear benefits against their expected needs.

Before enrolling, consumers should review current premiums, covered services, copays, allowances, exclusions, and provider requirements. State-specific plan documents confirm the exact benefits available. Questions about specific retailers, eyewear products, or services should be addressed with VSP or the participating provider before making a purchase.

Better Business Advice's coverage of the topic highlights the importance of understanding the distinction between Medicare medical benefits and separate routine vision coverage. Medicare Open Enrollment offers a timely opportunity to review healthcare expenses, while a careful comparison of standalone policies can help consumers assess whether additional vision coverage fits their budget and needs.

For the full review, visit Better Business Advice.

*Check your Medicare plan to see if your vision care needs are covered and/or if a VSP Individual Vision Plan is right for you. VSP Individual Vision Plans do not coordinate benefits with Medicare or any other plan.

VSP Vision Care provides members with access to affordable eye care and eyewear through thousands of network providers. As the only national not-for-profit company in vision care, we reinvest our profits back into the communities we serve so that everyone can enjoy a lifetime of well-being.

data.title: SAP reportedly to cut 10,000 jobs. It marks the latest in a brutal year for tech layoffs.
data.description:
By Nora Redmond

SAP is reportedly discussing cutting at least 10,000 jobs.

SAP is reportedly considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs in a heavy year of layoffs for the technology industry, withe more workforce reductions in the U.S. than any other sector.

The German software company (SAP) (XE:SAP) is discussing a restructuring set to affect about 9% to 10% of its overall workforce as it seeks to transition the business amid the artificial-intelligence boom, according to people familiar with the matter who spoke to Bloomberg. The total number of job cuts has not yet been finalized and could change following negotiations with employee representative groups.

"The business environment in which we operate is changing rapidly through AI, and we are continuously reviewing how our organization and workforce need to evolve to remain successful. As part of this ongoing transformation, roles and functions will naturally change over time. Beyond this, no decisions have been made regarding any further measures," an SAP spokesperson told MarketWatch.

The company is Germany's biggest by market capitalization, with a value of around EUR226.67 billion ($248.49 billion). It marks the latest of the European country's major blue-chip companies to contemplate significant headcount reductions, with carmaker Volkswagen (XE:VOW) planning to slash 100,000 jobs and engineering firm Thyssenkrupp (XE:TKA) shedding 4,000 roles.

And the trend extends beyond Germany, with the tech industry as a whole experiencing a wave of layoffs from the beginning of the year right through to the end as more capital is allocated to the development of AI - and as the tool becomes more capable of performing complex human tasks.

The sector accounts for 28% of total job cuts in the U.S. in 2026, making it responsible for more layoffs than any other industry, according to October's Challenger, Gray and Christmas layoff report. Tech companies announced that they were axing 5,576 roles last month, the lowest in the year so far, yet still an increase of 21% year-on-year.

Through October, tech has been responsible for 171,501 layoffs, already exceeding 154,445 cuts the sector accounted for in the entirety of 2025. And, as the report only includes employees who accept an offer in cases of voluntary redundancy programs, Microsoft's voluntary exit offer to 60,000 workers has not even been included in the figures.

"These offers tend to signal more layoffs to come. Voluntary exit offers are a softer way to shrink. They let a company reduce headcount while giving employees a choice and a cushion," wrote Andy Challenger, chief revenue officer.

-Nora Redmond

data.title: Moody's Upgrades Vietnam's Sovereign Rating to Ba1
data.description:
By Jihye Lee

Moody's Ratings upgraded Vietnam's sovereign credit rating by one notch to Ba1 from Ba2, citing improving governance and the economy's shift toward higher-value-added industries.

The ratings company on Friday also changed its outlook to stable from positive. Institutional overhauls, robust growth prospects and a more diversified economy have strengthened Vietnam's ability to withstand shocks, Moody's said.

"Reforms have streamlined public administration and judicial processes, strengthened accountability and anticorruption controls and improved the regulatory environment," Moody's said, pointing to governance as a key driver of the ratings upgrade.

However, rapid credit growth and high leverage continue to pose risks to financial stability, it added. Vulnerabilities in Vietnam's banking sector and institutional risks may weaken Vietnam's credit profile, Moody's said.

data.title: This investment strategist is 100% in cash - and warns that buying the Nasdaq dip is like catching a falling knife
data.description:
By Jules Rimmer

42 Macro strategist thinks the Fed is three moves away from neutral

A career spent catching knives will be a brief one, says 42 Macro's Darius Dale

Just because Nasdaq briefly entered bear-market territory this week, that's no reason in itself to buy stock, is the message from the head of one investment research service.

Darius Dale, founder and chief executive of the investment research boutique 42 Macro has advice for investors who think it is: "Research shows that if you try to make a career out of catching falling knives, you're not going to have a career for very long.'

For Dale, far better to "be the second investor in a confirmed trade, not the first in an unconfirmed."

Dale was articulating his extremely cautious opinions on the David Lin Report podcast, aired Thursday,. Opinions that are so cautious, his KISS model portfolio (standing for "Keep it Simple and Systematic") shifted into 80% cash at the end of September and has for the last few weeks actually been 100% cash.

Justifying this bearish stance he replied to Lin's suggestion that one might just buy stocks because they've declined so much, "that's just not what we do. We have a risk management system that's looking for signals to confirm" a move like that.

The main reason for Dale's extreme caution is that the Federal Reserve, for credibility's sake, needs to hike in December, and probably again in March to shore up its inflation-fighting credentials. "If they don't hike in December, they might as well close the institution," he says. Right now, Dale's models calculate the Fed is three 25-basis point hikes away from a policy that could be described as neutral.

The Fed is expected to tighten into the first half of 2027

It's not just inflation forcing rates higher. Dale's Wall Street contacts indicate to him that the hyperscalers (AMZN) (GOOG) (MSFT) may issue as much as $1 trillion in debt over the next few years, triple what they raised this year. That adds upward pressure on the cost of capital.

Dale cites many factors suggesting the economy is running too hot, highlighting supercore personal consumption expenditure at 4.2% year-over-year. It may take then, in Dale's opinion, until the second half of 2027 for the narrative to shift from a restrictive to a more accommodative approach, creating a policy tailwind to support equities, metals and bitcoin (BTCUSD).

As well as its KISS model, 42 Macro also runs a "Dr Mo" portfolio, representing a discretionary risk management overlay that interprets signals from 80 different factors, including rates, currencies, stocks and commodities. Late September, that model too suggested a reduction in beta - stocks that exaggerate market moves in any direction - and to move up the quality spectrum.

Dale is concerned that markets are having to digest a slowdown in the artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout, specifically identifying data centers as well as the situation with Nvidia (NVDA) and issues surrounding its chip sales. Yet, he observes earnings forecasts for 2027 are still at or near the cycle highs.

At some point, when markets are convinced about the direction of rates, the markets may well rip, Dale says and when they do the things to buy will be semiconductors SOX, Korea KR:180721, Taiwan XX:180909, base metals , bitcoin and other crypto currencies. For now, though, "the signals are not telling us to put on risk."

-Jules Rimmer
